name: SQLAlchemy
covers: Rerail's own SQLAlchemy rules, from the SQLAlchemy 2.0 docs and migration guide, for safe sessions, transactions, queries and relationship loading.

rules.title: SQLAlchemy practice: an except handler swallows a failed commit() or flush() and the session is used again without rollback()

caught.text:
import logging

from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import Tag

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def import_tags(engine, names: list[str]) -> None:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        for name in names:
            try:
                session.add(Tag(name=name))
                session.commit()
            except IntegrityError:
                log.warning("duplicate tag %s", name)
                continue

passes.text:
import logging

from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import Tag

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def import_tags(engine, names: list[str]) -> None:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        for name in names:
            try:
                session.add(Tag(name=name))
                session.commit()
            except IntegrityError:
                session.rollback()
                log.warning("duplicate tag %s", name)

rules.title: SQLAlchemy practice: a loop over ORM rows that reads a lazily loaded collection of every row

caught.text:
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import Order


def line_counts(session: Session) -> list[int]:
    counts = []
    for order in session.scalars(select(Order)):
        counts.append(len(order.lines))
    return counts

with.text:
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Order(Base):
    __tablename__ = "orders"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    lines: Mapped[list["Line"]] = relationship(back_populates="order")


class Line(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lines"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    order_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("orders.id"))
    order: Mapped[Order] = relationship(back_populates="lines")

rules.title: SQLAlchemy practice: writes on a connection from engine.connect() are committed, or the connection comes from engine.begin()

caught.text:
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, MetaData, String, Table, create_engine, insert

engine = create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://app@db/app")
metadata = MetaData()
users = Table("users", metadata, Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True), Column("name", String(80)))


def add_user(name: str) -> None:
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(insert(users).values(name=name))

passes.text:
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, MetaData, String, Table, create_engine, insert

engine = create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://app@db/app")
metadata = MetaData()
users = Table("users", metadata, Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True), Column("name", String(80)))


def add_user(name: str) -> None:
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(insert(users).values(name=name))
        conn.commit()
